Replace the per-row lookup with one batched fetch — eager-load the relation (`joinedload`/equivalent) or a single `JOIN` / `WHERE id IN (...)` query.

Also paginate the table and select only needed columns, with an index on the foreign key.

p04-auto.answer:
You're likely missing a `CHECK` on a `state/status` column: bare `TEXT` means the DB knows 0 legal states while your code enum defines N.

Your nightly `DELETE ... WHERE state IN (...)` enumerates G < N, so terminal-but-unlisted states accumulate forever and runtime grows past sunrise.

Check your rollup/metrics filter too — it usually shares the same omission, hiding growth until disk fills.

And `DELETE` never reclaims disk without `VACUUM` — confirm autovacuum keeps up, the collector actually runs in prod, and omitted variants are truly terminal.

p11-auto.answer:
After a redesign, start at Layer 1: crawlability → indexation, per dependency chain — uncrawlable pages make content fixes worthless.

Check `robots.txt` for unintentional blocks, XML sitemap for stale URLs, Search Console index coverage vs expected count, redirect chains/loops from old URLs, and canonical tags pointing correctly.

p11-high.answer:
After a redesign, start at Layer 1: crawlability → indexation, per dependency chain — uncrawlable pages make content fixes worthless.

Check `robots.txt` for unintentional blocks, XML sitemap for stale URLs, Search Console index coverage vs expected count, redirect chains/loops from old URLs, and canonical tags pointing at retired URLs.

Then Layer 2: HTTPS/mixed content, mobile rendering, URL structure changes, and Core Web Vitals (LCP <2.5s, INP <200ms, CLS <0.1).

Most post-redesign drops trace to blocked crawls, broken redirects, or deindexed pages — not content.
